short: The unprecedented trial and beheading of the English monarch, fundamentally challenging the divine right of kings.
full:
On 30 January 1649, King Charles I was executed outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall, London. Following his defeat in the Second English Civil War, the radicalized New Model Army and the Rump Parliament had put the king on trial for high treason, accusing him of using his power for personal interest rather than the good of the nation. Charles refused to recognize the legality of the court, arguing that no earthly power could judge a divinely appointed monarch.

The king faced his death with widely noted dignity, cementing his image as a martyr among Royalist supporters. His execution sent shockwaves across Europe, proving that a sitting monarch could be held accountable by his subjects. The regicide completely dismantled the traditional English constitution, inaugurating an eleven-year interregnum where England was governed as a republic and eventually a military dictatorship.
